en: And so you'll see higher token spend, slower times, lower accuracy.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: I had months where I was like, is anyone going to care about paper?
zh: 有几个月我在想，会有人在 care paper 吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it was like, oh yeah, people do care.

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, this is great.

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really taking off.

speaker: Unknown
en: It was the thing I was going to do anyway.
zh: 这是我无论如何都要做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was very much the thing I was going to do anyway, which I really believe starting a startup, you should do that.
zh: 这非常是我无论如何都要做的事情，我真的相信创业，你应该这样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: You should do the thing you're going to do anyway.
zh: 你应该做你无论如何都要做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: You should do the thing where you have founder market fit.
zh: 你应该做你有创始人市场匹配度的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for me, this is where I had the strongest founder market fit because I love building tools for creative professionals.
zh: 对我来说，这是我有最强创始人市场匹配度的地方，因为我热爱为创意专业人士构建工具。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: And so far, so good.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: The handoff will be better.
zh: 交接过程会更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: It turns out if you build a great handoff for humans, you've also built a great handoff for agents because agents understand HTML and CSS and it's in their training data.
zh: 结果证明，如果你为人类构建了很棒的交接，你同时也为智能体构建了很棒的交接，因为智能体理解 HTML 和 CSS，而且这些在它们的训练数据中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when you ask an agent to work with a paper file, it's literally just reading the CSS out and agents know exactly what to do with it.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我们试图基本上用视觉界面来扩展智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes I think ePaper is a design tool, but it's also this visual interface for agents.
zh: 有时我认为 Paper 是一个设计工具，但它也是智能体的这种视觉界面。

speaker: Unknown
en: We see sales folks, engineers, all kinds of people are using it because prompting isn't always the best input mechanism for agents.

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes you want to drag and draw, and it's just faster to be able to do direct manipulation.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: The best compliment you can give me is that paper is really great software.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 所以我想为世界带来更多这样的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I want to help designers and people with taste keep up with all of the software that's being created.
zh: 所以我想帮助设计师和有品味的人跟上所有正在创建的软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so giving them a tool that can move at the speed of prompting and of the agents, rather than being just pulled into an IDE or just pulled into prototyping, but being able to still do the traditional design work at a faster pace, I think it's really, really important.
zh: 所以给他们一个能够以提示和智能体的速度移动的工具，而不是仅仅被拉进一个 IDE 或仅仅被拉进原型制作，而是能够仍然以更快的速度做传统的设计工作，我认为这真的，真的很重要。

en: And then a couple of years after that, I just wanted to start back into creative tooling again.

en: And are there any lessons that you took from that experience that you're applying this time?

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, the make something people want is a great phrase.
zh: 你知道，做出人们想要的东西是一个很好的短语。

speaker: Unknown
en: And really, a lot of times with your product, it's like, what does my company need next?
zh: 实际上，很多时候对于你的产品来说，就像，我的公司接下来需要什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What would be like the best thing that possibly could happen to my company right now?
zh: 现在对我公司来说可能发生的最好的事情是什么？

en: At the beginning for us, that was like being part of the conversation, having Twitter followers.

en: Let's talk to users and then represent their values outwardly.

en: So a lot of times it's actually very simple.
zh: 所以很多时候实际上非常简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we make it too complicated.
zh: 我认为我们把它搞得太复杂了。

en: And we're trying to have these brilliant strategies for our companies.

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's like, what do you need next?
zh: 这就像，你接下来需要什么？

en: And just do the most straightforward thing you can possibly do to get there.
zh: 并且只做你可能做到的最直接的事情来达成目标。

en: And don't be scared to do things that sound hard.

en: Obviously, you've got to do them.
zh: 显然，你必须去做它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's the philosophy we've taken.
zh: 所以这就是我们要采取的哲学。

speaker: Unknown
en: Bottlenecks first.
zh: 瓶颈优先。

speaker: Unknown
en: Huge, huge philosophy I really believe in.
zh: 我非常相信的一个巨大的、巨大的哲学。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like for us right now, the bottleneck is early adopters are using paper.
zh: 就像对我们现在，瓶颈是早期采用者正在使用 Paper。

speaker: Unknown
en: The people that are more, you know, maybe not an early adopter type are very used to what they're doing now.
zh: 那些，你知道，可能不是早期采用者类型的人非常习惯于他们现在所做的事情。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 他们缺少像评论和组件这样的功能。

en: And so now our bottleneck is actually features again.

zh: 所以现在就像，好吧，那就是我们要去做的下一步。

en: And release that bottleneck to the business.

speaker: Unknown
en: And I did it all the way through the year.
zh: 而且我这一整年都坚持了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was so useful because I learned just how
zh: 这非常有用，因为我了解了

speaker: Unknown

en: You can't help that.

speaker: Unknown
en: You have a curse of knowledge.

speaker: Unknown
en: And so just staying rooted in user conversations is really important.

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.

speaker: Unknown
en: It gets harder and harder to do that as the company grows and scales also because there's so many other things that are vying for your time and pulling you in different directions and that seem important or hair on fire in the moment.

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But really it's those core fundamental things of build your product, talk to users.
zh: 但实际上，就是那些核心的基础事项，构建你的产品，与用户交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, exercise or whatever you need to do so you don't go crazy doing the first few things.
zh: 还有，你知道，锻炼或者做任何你需要做的事，这样你在做前几件事时不会发疯。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's the core of it for the life of the company, right?
zh: 但这就是公司在整个生命周期中的核心，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's it.
zh: 就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's cool to hear that you've done that from the very first day.

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm sure it is something that has been instilled culturally in your team now and that everybody is talking to users at this point.

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, yeah, yeah.

zh: 那个决策真的很棒。

en: Having an informed employee base, like I can't make every decision in the company.

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you can have your employees be really informed about users and what they actually want, you'll have good decisions being made all over, you know, all over the place.
zh: 所以如果你能让你的员工对用户以及他们真正想要的东西非常了解，你就能在各地，你知道，到处都能做出好的决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yeah, it's really important.
zh: 是的，这真的很重要。

zh: 嗯，我认为很多设计并没有改变。

zh: 同样，在组织内部，就像设计的功能作为一种探索问题空间、竞争分析、执行利益相关者等方式，仍然非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not seeing that change at all.
zh: 我们完全没有看到那种变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that function of design, I think, is sticking around.

en: Because I think that a lot of design is a very human problem, and the pixels at the end are like the output of the process.
